content.text: Stripe's availability map covers 46 countries. PayPal's risk engine flags accounts from Nigeria, Ghana, Pakistan, Bangladesh, and dozens of other markets before any human review occurs. Gumroad holds payouts for up to 30 days in certain regions. Lemon Squeezy and Paddle are unavailable across most of Africa, South Asia, and Latin America. These are not temporary oversights waiting to be corrected — they are deliberate structural decisions built into conventional [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/usdt-[[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/payment-options-ethiopian-digital-creators-explained-digital-creators-2|COREMERCH guide to payment]]-gateways-digital-products-explained-digital-[[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/how-creators-ghana-get-paid-online-what-actually-4|How Creators]]-16|payment]] infrastructure designed for Western banking systems. The solution is not finding a workaround inside this system. It is building on infrastructure that does not have the problem in the first place. That means GitHub Pages or Cloudflare Pages for hosting, Cloudflare Workers or Google Apps Script for backend logic, and NOWPayments for automatic on-chain payment verification. No platform can restrict access to a store that runs under your own accounts with no dependency on any payment processor.

This post is part of the COREMERCH infrastructure series. For the complete foundation — every component, every configuration step, and the full deployment sequence — read the pillar guide: The Complete Guide to Selling Digital Products Without Stripe at https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/comparing-real-options-selling-digital-products-without-stripe-2. content.text: What Each Option Actually Offers: Stripe alternatives

Stripe, PayPal, Gumroad, Lemon Squeezy, and Paddle each offer unique features for digital creators, but their availability is limited to specific countries, excluding a significant portion of the global community, whereas sovereign commerce infrastructure provides a comprehensive solution, enabling creators to sell digital products without geographical constraints, using platforms like GitHub Pages, Cloudflare Workers, and Supabase for a fully operational online store.
How They Handle Restricted Countries

Gumroad's payout delays, Payhip's withdrawal restrictions, and Lemon Squeezy's geographic unavailability all stem from the same root cause: these platforms operate within the traditional financial system. They process payments through Stripe or PayPal on the backend, which means they inherit every restriction those processors impose. When Stripe does not support your country, Gumroad cannot pay you out — regardless of what the platform's feature list implies. Paddle operates as a merchant of record, which creates additional compliance requirements that make it functionally unavailable in most of Africa, South Asia, and Latin America. These are not platform-level problems. They are financial system problems that only infrastructure built outside that system can solve.
Payment Speed, Fees, and Real Costs

While conventional platforms charge transaction fees and may hold funds, sovereign commerce infrastructure, through solutions like NOWPayments, offers automatic on-chain crypto payment verification with a minimal 0.5% fee, ensuring that creators receive their earnings promptly and in full, without the risk of account suspension or fund withholding, as seen with PayPal, which can hold funds for up to 180 days.
Sovereign commerce infrastructure empowers creators with full control over their digital sales.
Ownership, Automation, and Delivery

The asymmetric risk of platform dependency becomes concrete only when the platform acts. While a PayPal or Stripe account is functioning normally, the risk feels theoretical and distant. When it stops functioning — through suspension, policy change, or geographic restriction enforcement — the creator loses their revenue channel instantly, often with funds already inside the platform that cannot be withdrawn. The conventional appeals process rarely reverses these decisions because the original decision was made algorithmically and the human review process operates on the platform's timeline and criteria, not yours. Sovereign infrastructure eliminates this asymmetry entirely. Your Cloudflare Pages storefront cannot be suspended by a payment processor's compliance decision. Your wallet cannot be frozen by anyone.
Which Architecture to Choose Based on Your Situation

The storefront in a COREMERCH deployment is a static site hosted on GitHub Pages or Cloudflare Pages. It costs nothing to host. It scales to any traffic level automatically. It cannot be taken down by a payment platform's compliance decision because the hosting and the payment layer are completely separate infrastructure. Your buyer experience is clean and professional — a product page, a crypto checkout with QR code generation and live price feeds, and an automatic delivery email within 30 seconds of payment. Every component runs under your own accounts. If COREMERCH closed tomorrow, every store deployed would continue running exactly as it does today. That is what infrastructure ownership means.
How do I sell digital products if Stripe is not available in my country?

The direct answer is NOWPayments combined with a sovereign commerce stack. NOWPayments is a crypto payment processor that requires no KYC from merchants and no account creation from buyers. It supports over 300 coins, charges 0.5% per transaction, and sends a webhook to your backend the moment payment confirms on-chain. Your backend — a Cloudflare Worker in Stack 02, a Google Apps Script Web App in Stack 01 — receives the webhook, verifies the transaction hash on the blockchain, logs the order, generates a receipt, and sends the delivery email automatically. There is no platform that can suspend your access, no compliance team that can flag your account, no payout schedule that delays your revenue, and no company that can change the rules on you tomorrow.
Traditional platforms like Stripe and PayPal have limited geographical availability.

Your Deployment Checklist

To deploy a sovereign commerce infrastructure, start by selecting a hosting platform like GitHub Pages or Cloudflare Pages, then set up backend logic using Cloudflare Workers or Google Apps Script, next, choose an order storage solution such as Supabase or Google Sheets, followed by configuring file delivery through Google Drive or Cloudflare R2, and finally, integrate NOWPayments for automatic crypto payment verification, ensuring a fully operational online store with minimal fees and maximum control.
